body:
Maya (Sales): Customer (ACME) POC failing with 413 when they POST full session JSON (~12MB). They want a one-page workaround.
Carlos (SE): 413 = gateway rejecting body. Ask region + paste sanitized request + raw response.
Maya (Sales): They hit us-west. Client output: 
```
POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Content-Length: 12582912

HTTP/1.1 413 Request Entity Too Large
{"error":"request too large"}
```
Jamal (Support): Confirmed: hosted gateways enforce ~10MB. This blocks transport before model/token checks.
Liu (Platform Eng): We don't bump prod gateway per-customer. Options: upload+pointer, chunking, summarization, or Dedicated with higher ingress.
Priya (Eng Oncall): Opening a ticket to see if a temporary routing workaround is feasible, but it'll need infra + security approvals. Short-term: use /v1/upload or presigned S3.
Carlos (SE): Share minimal example flow for upload+reference: 
```
# 1) POST /v1/upload -> {"upload_id":"u123","presigned_url":"..."}
# 2) PUT file to presigned_url (full JSON)
# 3) POST /v1/generate {"transcript_ref":"upload:u123","last_n":20}
```
Maya (Sales): Customer asks "can you turn this up for a demo?"
Liu (Platform Eng): For Hosted: no quick toggle. For Dedicated POC we can increase ingress (requires provisioning and billing change). Ballpark: $1k/day, lead time 48-96h.
Jamal (Support): Note: gzip helps when uploading to /v1/upload; it does not bypass the /v1/generate gateway limit. Also Transfer-Encoding chunked won't avoid the configured limit.
Carlos (SE): Even if transport is resolved, watch model token windows. Ask which model and estimate token count; otherwise they'll hit truncation.
Maya (Sales): I'll present three options to ACME: 1) upload+pointer (fast), 2) client chunk & stitch, 3) Dedicated POC bump (sales+ops). Linking ticket INF-4501.
deploy-bot: Ticket INF-4501 created by Priya (Eng Oncall)
